claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

First, could you tell me: **Do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 4 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your 4-year-old son Alex who lives with you in the UK.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex?** By this I mean, do you have the main responsibility for him - for example, do you provide his day-to-day care, make decisions about his upbringing, and meet his needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm his parent and I look after him every day. I take care of all his needs - you know, feeding him, getting him dressed, taking him to nursery, that sort of thing. I make all the decisions about his care and upbringing as well.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that.

Now I need to ask: **Are you currently living in the UK yourself?** And if so, do you have the right to reside here (for example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, indefinite leave to remain, or another immigration status that allows you to live here)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester. And yes, I have the right to live here, no issues with that at all.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him, so no one else has put in a claim.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that.

One final question: **Do you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000 per year?** 

(Note: If you or your partner earns between £50,000 and £60,000, you can still claim Child Benefit but may need to pay some of it back through the High Income Child Benefit Charge. If either of you earns over £60,000, you'd need to pay back the full amount through tax.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us earns anywhere near that amount. We're well under £50,000, so that shouldn't be an issue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ Alex is 4 years old (under 16)
✓ You are responsible for Alex and provide his day-to-day care
✓ Alex lives with you in the UK
✓ You live in the UK and have the right to reside here
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
✓ Your household income is under £50,000, so you won't need to pay any High Income Child Benefit Charge

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. You can proceed with making a claim for Alex. Child Benefit is usually paid every 4 weeks, and you'll receive payments for Alex until he turns 16 (or up to age 20 if he stays in approved education or training).

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
